thread:
Maya: Hey folks — quick follow-up from the all-hands. Wanted to surface the sales pipeline + GTM questions that came up. We'll answer live here.
Sam: Quick snapshot — pipeline up 28% QoQ, four enterprise deals in late stages (>$200k ARR each). We expect 2–3 to close next quarter.
Julia: Can you clarify which verticals are driving the pipeline growth?
Sam: Mainly fintech and SaaS platform integrations. Fintech deals are pushing for on-prem/private deployments due to compliance.
Rachel: Partnerships update — Channel partner pilot with Databridge is starting next month; expect 2-3 joint prospects in the funnel.
Devon: On GTM focus: we're doubling down on developer-first demos and prescriptive cost/latency benchmarks in sales plays. That means more collateral + benchmark runs for prospects.
Maya: Question from the floor — how is pricing going to change for Dedicated customers?
Allen: No headline pricing change this quarter. We're piloting a simplified seatless model for dedicated reserves with a few customers; if successful, we may roll out as an option next Q.
Julia: For the seatless pilot — what's the criteria to be eligible?
Sam: Eligibility: committed spend > $150k/year, ability to sign a 12mo contract, and acceptance of our standard SLA. We'll route candidates through Sales Ops.
AnonymousUser: Any updates on partner revenue share and co-sell credits?
Rachel: Revenue share stays standard for now; co-sell credits will be experiment-based per partner. For Databridge pilot we're offering enhanced co-sell support (lead sharing, bundled PoC credit).
Maya: How are we protecting gross margins while pursuing enterprise deals that ask for lots of custom work?
Devon: Two-pronged approach — productize common integrations (reusable templates) and offer funded services for bespoke work. That keeps professional services from eroding unit economics.
Sam: Also using Redwood Optimize to propose quantization & batching recommendations pre-SOW to show cost savings up front. Helps close while protecting margins.
Julia: Can the Partnerships team share a short checklist for Sales to qualify partner-led opportunities?
Rachel: Yep, I'll publish a one-pager in the partners channel by EOD with criteria: partner-ready solution, co-sell motion identified, expected ARR, technical fit, and legal red flags.
Maya: Any regrets or things we should course-correct from this quarter's GTM experiments?
Sam: We were slow to standardize benchmark artifacts; sales teams had to recreate them per deal. Fixing with a shared benchmark repo/shortlist of configurations.
Allen: Product note — we'll expose precomputed benchmark results in Console for common models/configs to speed demos. Target: next release.
Maya: Final — for customers asking about region redundancy and cross-region failover for Dedicated, what's the current askback?
Devon: Customers want cross-region failover for DR but not always active-active. We're proposing automated warm-standby with failover playbooks. Currently a Professional Services offering; long-term roadmapped.
Sam: I'll follow up with a short thread to Sales with the updated qualifying criteria and the benchmark checklist.
Rachel: I'll post the Databridge pilot README and partner one-pager later today.
all-hands-bot: Reminder — Q&A summary will be attached to the all-hands notes (link posted) and follow-ups assigned as action items. :white_check_mark:
Maya: Thanks everyone — keep questions coming here or ping me/Devon directly.
